subject: Post-demo: acceptance gates, regression guardrails & next steps for ClearPay trial
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@clearpay.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearPay Data Team <data-team@clearpay.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks for the demo — model recommendations & acceptance criteria

Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo today — the team found the latency and streaming chops compelling. A few follow-ups from our side so we can get to a short trial / benchmark run: 

1) Can you summarize which open models you recommend we try first and a Redwood-provided baseline to compare against?
2) We need an initial acceptance criteria doc (high-level thresholds) that we can use to gate go/no-go for the trial. Focus on: intent classification accuracy, entity extraction F1, hallucination incidents per 1k responses, and p95 latency.
3) Please share the prompt bundle and any suggested retrieval/context strategy so we can run consistent tests.
4) Any security/compliance caveats for a short hosted trial (data residency, logs, retention) would be good to see.

If we can get those by EOD Wednesday PT we can stand up the trial next week.

-Maya

--
Maya Singh
Head of Data Platforms, ClearPay
maya@clearpay.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: meeting-recording.mp4 (video, 28MB)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@clearpay.com>
Cc: ClearPay Data Team <data-team@clearpay.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — model recommendations & acceptance criteria

Maya — thanks for the clear ask and for setting timelines. High-level recap + proposed next steps below.

Recap from call
- Primary workload: transaction categorization + named entity extraction from short chat-like user queries and uploaded receipts.
- Volume profile: 100k monthly active users, 50 req/s burst, median prompt length ~ 120 tokens, retrieval context up to ~1k tokens.
- Risk areas: entity recall on abbreviations, occasional hallucination on merchant normalization, and latency sensitivity on mobile flows.

Initial model recommendations (trial shortlist)
- Open-first candidates (fast path):
  * LlamaX-13B-q4 (open) — good balance of generation quality and quantized latency; strong for intent/slot extraction with tuned prompts.
  * OpenRed-7B-int8 (open) — lower-cost candidate useful to test cost-quality tradeoffs on high QPS.
- Redwood baseline:
  * Redwood-Standard-3B (internal-optimized variant) — our usually recommended baseline for structured-extraction tasks; optimized kernels and prefix caching enabled.

Suggested acceptance gates (proposal)
- Intent accuracy (macro): >= 0.88 on our shared eval set
- Entity extraction F1 (key fields): >= 0.82
- Hallucination rate: < 2 incidents per 1k responses (definition: asserted factual claims not present in context)
- Latency (p95 generation excluding network): < 250 ms
- Cost: per-1M-token proxy estimate (we'll provide comparison numbers in the benchmark CSV)

Trial plan & artifacts
- We will: provide a prompt bundle and evaluation harness (unit tests + scoring) and run 3 models for 48-hour structured runs.
- Deliverables by Redwood by Wed EOD PT: prompt-bundle v1, acceptance-gates PDF, initial benchmark template.
- Kickoff target: Mon 10/11 for the trial window (can be adjusted).

Security/compliance notes
- Hosted trial: logs retained per agreed retention and can be scrubbed on demand; we will provide a short security appendix for trial mode (data residency, encryption-in-transit & at-rest, minimal logs). Neha will add details.

Attachments included: clearpay-prompt-bundle-v1.md, initial-benchmarks-summary.csv, acceptance-gates-checklist.pdf

Next steps (actions)
- Marissa: run baseline vs LlamaX-13B and OpenRed-7B locally/hosted and populate the benchmark CSV (due Thu EOD).
- Neha: security appendix and trial constraints (due Wed EOD).
- Karthik: coordinate SOW/DocuSign if ClearPay wants reserved capacity after trial.

If that aligns, we’ll share the Drive folder + HubSpot task.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Attachments: clearpay-prompt-bundle-v1.md (markdown, 12 KB); initial-benchmarks-summary.csv (csv, 18 KB); acceptance-gates-checklist.pdf (pdf, 45 KB)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 18:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Thanks for the demo — model recommendations & acceptance criteria

Team — forwarding ClearPay's request and our proposed gates. Need quick alignment so we can hit the Wed deliverable. TL;DR assignments below.

Context (quick): ClearPay wants to run a short trial next week. They care most about intent accuracy + entity extraction. They asked for prompts, acceptance gates, and a short benchmark run across an open candidate set + our baseline.

Ask (please):
- Marissa: run the three-model comparison (Redwood-Standard-3B, LlamaX-13B-q4, OpenRed-7B-int8) on the evaluation harness I attached. Focus metrics: intent accuracy, entity F1 per slot, hallucination count, and p95 generation latency. Put results into initial-benchmarks-summary.csv. Target: Thu EOD (accelerate if possible).
- Neha: draft a 1-pager security appendix for trial (data handling, retention, logs access, any limitations on hosted trial). Deliver Wed EOD so I can share with Maya.
- Dylan: take the prompt bundle and produce a prompt-playbook with suggested retrieval snippets and temperature/sampling settings for each test. Also include a short list of QA tests that will surface hallucinations. Due: Wed EOD.

Notes: keep runs deterministic where possible (seeded runs), record p95 excluding network time, and include raw example responses for 10 edge-case prompts (we'll send those).

I’ll loop in legal if ClearPay pushes reserved capacity language after trial. Reply-all with a one-line ack and ETA.

— Karthik

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Thanks for the demo — model recommendations & acceptance criteria

Karthik — ACK and plan below. Quick hits from initial run (local cluster, dev harness):

What I ran
- Small seed eval: 1k examples (mix of intents + entity-heavy receipts) using the harness in the Drive folder. Models: Redwood-Standard-3B (opt kernels), LlamaX-13B-q4, OpenRed-7B-int8.

Preliminary findings (summary)
- Intent accuracy: LlamaX-13B-q4 = 0.885, Redwood-Standard-3B = 0.892, OpenRed-7B-int8 = 0.861
- Entity extraction F1 (key slots: merchant, total_amount, date): LlamaX = 0.79, Redwood = 0.84, OpenRed = 0.75
- Hallucinations (per 1k): LlamaX = 3.1, Redwood = 1.4, OpenRed = 4.2
- p95 generation latency (ms, local infra): LlamaX = 230, Redwood = 210, OpenRed = 190

Interpretation & recommendation
- On intent, LlamaX is close to parity but trails on structured entity extraction. Redwood-Standard is ahead on slot F1 and lower hallucination rate.
- Short-term mitigation: add focused prompt templates for entity extraction and a light retrieval layer (top-3 receipts by similarity) — this narrows the entity gap in tests by ~0.04 F1 in our small run.

Deliverables I’ll attach to the Drive by midday: full CSV with per-example scores, 10 raw example responses flagged for hallucination, and a short README describing the harness.

Next internal asks
- Neha: confirm whether the trial retention settings we discussed earlier are acceptable for ClearPay's legal team; if not, propose the minimum changes.
- Dylan: please draft the prompt-playbook and include the retrieval snippet — I can test once you share.

I’ll prioritize a larger 10k-sample run after we align on the prompt-playbook — should give statistically firmer numbers.

— Marissa
Director, Applied ML | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments (will be uploaded): initial-benchmarks-summary.csv (seed-run), raw-hallucination-examples.json (stub), run-readme.md
